Physics hand-checked: strain is the change in dimension per unit original dimension; it is a ratio of two like quantities, so it carries no unit and no dimensions.

insider_note: Students often forget to state that strain has no unit — that line alone carries the second mark.

page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: Strain — the definition
lines: Strain is the change in dimension
per unit original dimension of a
steps.margin_note: Say "change in dimension per unit original dimension" in full — a vague "strain is deformation" does not earn this mark.
steps.why: Dimension here covers length, volume or shape, so this one definition covers longitudinal, volume and shearing strain alike.
common_mistakes: Defining strain only in terms of length change, which covers longitudinal strain but not volume or shearing strain.
Confusing strain with stress — strain is the deformation, stress is the force per unit area causing it.
steps.memory_tip: Strain is how much a body changed, per how much it started with.

steps.label: Formula and unit
lines: dimension. It is a ratio, so it has

lines.text: Strain = Δx/x — no unit, no dimensions.

steps.margin_note: State clearly that strain has no unit — it is the ratio of two lengths (or volumes), so the units cancel.
steps.why: Both quantities in the ratio carry the same unit, so they cancel and strain is left as a pure number.
common_mistakes: Giving strain a unit such as m or m³.
Writing the formula without saying it is a ratio with no unit.
steps.memory_tip: Same units on top and bottom cancel out — strain has none.
